# humanizer-lint

> Deterministic, zero-dependency universal multi-language stylometric prose linter and closed-loop AI text humanizer. Native `Intl.Segmenter` supports local word and sentence segmentation in the browser and Node.js.

`humanizer-lint` measures the finished draft instead of trusting a prompt alone. It reports configured lexical, rhythm, vocabulary, structural, and morphology diagnostics so a writer or agent can revise the exact text and verify it locally.

## Quick Install & Usage

- Agent skill install: `npx skills add yanstd888/humanizer-lint`
- Standalone CLI: `npx humanizer-lint --file draft.md --lang auto --json`
- Stdin pipe: `cat draft.md | npx humanizer-lint --stdin --json`
- Web playground: [https://humanizer.aiclub.ai.id/](https://humanizer.aiclub.ai.id/)

## Language tiers

- **Tier 1 — rule packs:** `en`, `id`, `es`, `ms`, `fr`, `de`, `pt`, and `zh` run universal stylometry plus their bundled lexical packs. Indonesian also applies its morphology checks.
- **Tier 2 — universal:** `universal` and other ISO 639-1 inputs run burstiness, adjacent rhythm delta, adaptive MATTR, paragraph symmetry, repeated starters, and compression-ratio checks. CJK inputs use a default MATTR target of `0.68`; other fallback languages use `0.72`.

Use `--lang auto` to select a supported pack only when the script or stopword evidence is strong, `--lang <ISO-639-1>` to request a language, or `--lang universal` to force Tier 2.

## Core Mathematical Metrics

- **Global Burstiness (CV):** Coefficient of variation (`standard deviation / mean`) over sentence lengths. Default long-text target: `CV >= 0.45`; on 8+ sentence text, also require at least `15%` short sentences (6 words or fewer) and `10%` long sentences (26 words or more).
- **Adjacent Rhythm Delta:** Mean absolute word-count difference between neighboring sentences. Default target: `>= 4`.
- **Adaptive MATTR:** Moving-average type-token ratio using an adaptive window up to 50 words. Default targets: `>= 0.72` for Indonesian and `>= 0.74` for English.
- **Morphological & lexical rules:** Detects configured English clichés and Indonesian translationese, nominalization, and passive-density patterns.
